Combined company expected to advance differentiated oral obesity franchise led by CX11, a clinical-stage, once-daily oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist (“RA”), and CX12, a preclinical oral small-molecule amylin receptor agonist.

CX11 has demonstrated clinically meaningful weight loss and a generally favorable tolerability profile across Phase 2 obesity studies in the United States. Following an End-of-Phase 2 meeting, Corxel US has aligned with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) on key elements of CX11’s regulatory path and Phase 3 trial design.

Institutional investors have committed to a private investment in public equity (“PIPE”) of approximately $300 million, with participation from new and existing investors including RTW Investments, New Enterprise Associates (NEA), SR One, Mirae Asset Capital Life Science, HBM Healthcare Investments (Cayman) Ltd., Nantahala Capital, Coastlands Capital, LifeSci Venture Partners, Invus, TCGX, RA Capital Management, Propel Bio, SilverArc Capital and a large healthcare mutual fund.
Transaction expected to provide approximately $377 million in gross proceeds (prior to the payment of transaction costs and assuming no redemptions by Amanat shareholders).

Business combination expected to be completed in the first half of 2027. Proceeds expected to support the company through 2029, including funding the planned global Phase 3 development program for CX11 in obesity.
